  local first.
- The language is chosen before the first render and never changes while a
  page runs, so `t` works anywhere, including at a module's top level and in
  plain `.ts` files. `Trans` and `useLingui` from the macros need no
  provider (see `i18n.tsx`).
- Tests run in English, so a test that finds text by its English words keeps
  working.

### In the native code

- `_L("…")` gives a `wxString` for a window; `_u8L("…")` gives UTF-8 for
  JSON sent to a page.
- Translate when the text is used, never in a static initializer, which runs
  before the language is loaded. Mark such a table with `L("…")` and call
  `_L`/`_u8L` on the entry where it is shown.
- Use `format(_L("%1% is too close to others"), name)` rather than
  concatenation, and `_L_PLURAL` for counts; `// TRN` above a string tells
  the translator what it means.
- Every file that marks text is extracted: `update_catalogs.py` reads every
  `.cpp` and `.hpp` under `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin` except `Testing/`. Do not
  add JusPrin files to `localization/i18n/list.txt`.

result.output:
Translate JusPrin into upstream OrcaSlicer's 22 languages

JusPrin's own windows and its AI and Home pages showed English in every
language. Every string a person reads in them is now marked and translated
into the 22 languages upstream ships, in catalogs of the fork's own so that
taking an upstream release never conflicts in one:

- Localization/native/<lang>.po for native text, collected by
  Localization/update_catalogs.py (text upstream's template already has
  keeps upstream's translation) and merged by Brand/brand_catalogs.py into
  the catalog the app loads.
- Localization/pages/<lang>.po for both pages, through Lingui 5.9.5. The app
  passes its language as ?lang=; the page activates it before any module
  runs.

Text the model reads (prompts, skills, tool results), logs, error reports,
identifiers and names stay English. The translations are machine-made and
marked "# AI Translated"; entries a translator was unsure of also carry
"# Needs human review: <what to check>". Terms follow upstream's catalog
and the OrcaSlicer localization glossary.

Sentences that were built from translated pieces are now one message each,
with placeholders and plural forms, and render the same English. Other
changes the translation needed:

- Support/Translate.hpp: GUI-free code marks text with L() and translates it
  with translated() and translated_plural(), which the app installs.
- "Model" and "Search models" in the printer picker, and "Plate" in the
  add-printer form, have contexts of their own, apart from the AI model and
  the project plate.
- Numbers JusPrin shows use the app language's separators
  (Support/DecimalText on the native side, decimalText on the pages): a
  German app reads "Kobra 3 · 0,4 mm".

The rest are built in the C++ code and sent to the pages or native windows as finished English text. Two cases are the same bug as the printer chat's opening line: the filament chat's opening line ("I can help with settings for … in slot …") and the printer chat's notes. The full list, with file and line for each string, is in [i18n-unmarked-strings.md](i18n-unmarked-strings.md). I left it untracked.

**Page code:**
- The printer chat's opening line, in all five forms. That includes the reply chips "Yes, it is | How do I check?" and the fallback name "this printer".
- "Check the plan against what changed.": the Check plan button sends it as the person's own message, so it shows as their chat bubble.
- "… N more characters" in an action's opened details.

**C++ side, the biggest groups:**
- **Action titles in the chat's activity line** (about 85). These are lines like "Slice the plate", "Import <path>" and "Change N settings of X". Nothing translates them on the way to the page. The model reads them only through one tool, so they can be translated where they're shown. Some are also wrong in English, such as "Change 1 settings".
- **Printer chat notes and card errors** (about 50). They are written for the model ("The person added X from the printer list.") and drawn on screen word for word. Simply marking them would put "the person" on screen in every language, so each one needs a separate sentence for the person. The code already has hooks for that (`post_note`'s `for_model` argument and a card error's `details.shown`).
- **Plates pane "Couldn't do that" dialog** (about 40). It shows the workspace's error message as it is.
- **Undo-step names in the Changes rows** (about 15). "Gizmo-Place on Face" has to stay English because OrcaSlicer compares it, so it can only be translated where it's displayed.
- **Values that never get translated** (about 25). These are the default plate name "Plate N", setting values such as "On", "Off" and "Not set", and OrcaSlicer's English setting labels in the Changes rows and the All settings plate and object rows.
- **Errors when installing a printer** on Home's first-run step and in the add-printer form.

**This isn't one marking pass.** About 20 of these are errors a person can do nothing about, such as most of the chat's red error banners and the "can't happen" plates-pane messages. Under the error-handling rules in AGENTS.md, those should become the generic "Something went wrong" sentence plus a report, not translated sentences.

I left out text only the model reads, log lines and ids. I also left out the "Was doing" row in the error dialog, which stays English on purpose.

One possible bug turned up that I didn't test: `PrinterPanel.cpp:125` converts a translated label with `ToStdString()` instead of `ToUTF8()`, so a label with non-ASCII letters could reach the page garbled or empty.

---
name: ux-walkthrough-real-app-recipe
description: "How to drive the real built JusPrin app for a screenshot-per-step UX walkthrough (2026-10-28): scratch copies, the empty local_machines loop with the fake printer, why background app_* tools fail on Orca dialogs, and where screenshots land."
metadata:
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: 33551592-d22c-4161-9a14-9a22ef798541
  modified: 2026-10-28T13:12:42.393Z
---

On 2026-10-28 I walked six scenarios (open-and-print, fix-a-problem) through the real app with Opus 5.5 and published the critique at https://claude.ai/artifact/XyVvteGiKhiJ6apUx8rcmR (34 frames, scratch copy at scratchpad/ux/ of that session). Kenneth's steer: start from files people actually download (MakerWorld 3MFs carry a full Bambu profile: printer, print preset, filaments, colours, bed type, designer, licence), not from generated STLs. `~/Downloads` has Tape_4_3MF.3mf (A1 mini profile), find_my_hollow.3mf (P1S, 3 colours, 233 mm wide, too big for an A1 mini), arrow_headband.3mf (P1S), general_purpose_hook.STL (bare).

**Recipe that worked**
- `ditto` the built .app out of `build/arm64/src/RelWithDebInfo/` into the scratchpad before launching (another session's ninja can relink it underneath you); the bundle id is already unique (`io.jusprin.JusPrin`), no re-sign needed.
- `ditto` `~/Library/Application Support/JusPrin2` to a scratch `--datadir`; set `jusprin.fake_printer=true`, `presets.machine` to the saved "Bambu Lab A1 mini 2", write `jusprin/fake_printer.json`, delete `jusprin/mcp.json.lock`.
- **Clear `local_machines`.** Kenneth's conf carries a `local_machines` entry keyed by the empty string (old Moonraker experiment). With the fake Bambu agent on, `init_networking_callbacks`' connect callback calls `DeviceManager::set_selected_machine("")` in a loop ("same lan machine, dev_id =, disconnect and reconnect"), the main window disappears and the log grew 700 MB in two minutes. Clearing the map fixed it. The loop has no guard; see [[fake-bambu-printer-sim]] and [[harness-fake-printer-cleanup]].
- Background `app_*` tools cannot press OrcaSlicer's custom `Button`s (no AX action) and the hit test at the dialog's screen position reports "belongs to a different process". `request_full_control` + `computer_batch` works for everything, including the Agent web view and the macOS file chooser (`cmd+shift+g`, type the path, Return, Return). Re-front the app with `open_application` when another session's harness steals focus.
- Every `app_screenshot`/`computer_batch` screenshot is written as a JPEG under `~/.claude/projects/<project>/<session>/tool-results/mcp-computer-use-blob-*.jpg`; copy those for a report instead of fighting `screencapture`.
- The dev build (-O0) slices a 38 mm part in over a minute; wait 45–60 s before judging a slice.

**Why:** the first launch attempt looked like an app bug (blank window, title "Couldn't save") and cost ten minutes; the dialog-click refusals cost another ten.
**How to apply:** reuse this for any "walk through the app as a user" request; keep scenarios on downloaded files; write the critique per step as what the person knows / sees / finds confusing. Related: [[live-test-built-app-on-mac]], [[drive-app-with-posted-key-events]].

name: live-test-built-app-on-mac
description: "How to launch, see, and drive the locally built JusPrin app on the Mac: the shared bundle id binds tools to the wrong instance, and \"on another Space\" usually means the window is on the second monitor, not that the user is in full screen."
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: fa2d66ed-e217-440b-aae0-da4164953edc
  modified: 2026-11-01T19:29:08.107Z
---

Every build of the fork (and /Applications/OrcaSlicer.app) shares bundle id `com.softfever3d.orca-slicer`. The desktop-control tools resolve an app by bundle id and bind to whichever instance comes first, so `app_list_windows` returns `[]` and filtered screenshots hide the window you actually launched.

**Working recipe (2026-09-05):** `ditto` the built .app into the scratchpad, `plutil -replace CFBundleIdentifier -string com.jusprin.worktree-test`, `codesign --force --deep -s -`, then `open -n <copy>.app --args <model>` and `request_access` for the new id. `app_screenshot`/`app_click` then work and include popup menus. A display-scope `left_click` on the header did NOT open the fork's PopupWindow menus, but a background `app_click` did; take the pixel-level `zoom` with the display tools afterwards (call `app_release` first). Display-scope `Escape` does not close those popups; a click elsewhere does.

The MCP discovery file `~/Library/Application Support/JusPrin2/jusprin/mcp.json` points at the newest instance's `http://127.0.0.1:<port>/mcp`; `tests/mcp/probe.py`'s `call()` can drive real tools (e.g. `workspace_inspect`, then `report_slice_review` with sessionId/plateId/sliceResultId) to put the header into the Check-print state without lldb. lldb `expr` cannot call inline accessors like `status_row()`.

**Why:** On 2026-09-01 a verification pass screenshotted the stock app instead of the build; on 2026-09-05 the tools bound to another session's main-repo build.

**How to apply:** Confirm the pid with `pgrep -fl OrcaSlicer.app/Contents/MacOS`; never kill an instance you did not launch. `osascript` System Events by unix id still works to set `frontmost`. See [[jusprin-shell-phase-1-design]] and [[orca-inherited-teardown-crash]].

**"On another Space" usually means "on the other monitor."** Cost about ten turns on
2026-09-09 and produced a wrong report to Kenneth. `app_list_windows` returns
`is_off_space: true` and clicks are refused with "this window is on another Space";
`app_bring_to_current_space` then fails with "the user's current Space is a full-screen
app." Both messages are about Spaces, so the natural read is that the user is sitting in
a full-screen app — but with *Displays have separate Spaces* on, a window merely sitting
on the second monitor produces exactly the same symptoms. Kenneth was not in full screen;
the harness had opened on the Acer.

Tell them apart before saying anything to the user: take a **display-scope** screenshot
(`app_release`, then `computer_batch` screenshot). Its header names the monitor it
captured and lists the others — if the window shows up there, it is a monitor problem,
not a Space problem, and the display-scope tools can drive it immediately. Never conclude
"the user is in a full-screen app" from the background tools' error text alone.

The same flag also flaps: a window can read `is_off_space: false` and click fine, then
read `true` a minute later. Clicks delivered while it is true report `ok ... unverified`
and silently do nothing. **A click that reports "unverified" and changes nothing is not
evidence of an application bug** — on 2026-09-09 that nearly became a filed defect about
being unable to retry after a failed MCP connect. Re-verify on a reachable window before
concluding anything about the app.

**Prefer the shell harness over a re-signed app copy for Agent-panel work.**
`tests/shell/.../JusPrinShellHarness.app` already carries its own bundle id
(`io.jusprin.shell-harness`), so none of the bundle-id collision above applies, and
`--manual-unconfigured` lands directly on the dock's not-set-up state — one click from
the Agent setup chooser. Build target is `shell_integration_harness`, not `shell_harness`.

**Isolate `$HOME` when testing MCP client setup.** `Mcp::default_catalog_paths()` reads
`$HOME`, so the flow will happily rewrite the real `~/.cursor/mcp.json`. Launch with
`HOME=<scratch>` holding a `.cursor/mcp.json` fixture; detection, the diff, and the write
all follow it. Force a write failure with `chmod 444` on the file **and** `555` on its
directory — the directory alone is not enough.

**Re-signed copies trigger system prompts.** Each rebuild + ad-hoc re-sign changes the cdhash, so macOS re-asks for Downloads access (recent-project thumbnail load blocks in `fopen`) and Keychain access (agent runtime reads the API key). Both are prompts only the user can answer. Avoid them by running the binary directly (`nohup <copy>.app/Contents/MacOS/OrcaSlicer --datadir <scratch copy of JusPrin2 with recent_projects cleared> <model>`) with `OPENAI_API_KEY=<placeholder>` in the environment, which short-circuits the Keychain lookup in `AgentConfiguration.cpp`. Use `sample <pid>` on the main thread to see which prompt is blocking.

**Stale as of 2026-09-18 (branch claude/printer-conversation-panel-af11cb):** `load_agent_runtime` reads the key only from app config (`jusprin_agent` / `openai_api_key`); no env var or Keychain lookup exists there. In the shell harness, `OPENAI_API_KEY` only feeds the docked pane via `install_harness_agent`; the printer panel builds its own runtime from app config, so `--printer-live` writes the key into the run's throwaway conf. Pass it as `std::string`: `AppConfig::set(section, key, const char*)` silently picks the `bool` overload and stores `true` (seen as a 401 "key rejected"). The harness temp data dir then holds the real key: delete `/var/folders/*/*/T/jusprin-shell-*` dirs from those runs afterwards.

**Hands-on printer panel with a live model (2026-09-23, jusprin-newui, uncommitted at the time):** `--manual-live-agent` now also writes `OPENAI_API_KEY` into the run's app config, so Home → "+ Add printer" gets a live printer chat. Feed the key from `~/Library/Application Support/JusPrin2/JusPrin2.conf` (`jusprin_agent.openai_api_key`) via env without echoing it. Drive it with display-scope `computer_batch` clicks/typing (background `app_click` does nothing on the web view). The scripted `--printer-live` run hangs when the model doesn't pick the printer its next "tap" step expects; kill it. Afterwards `rm -rf` the run's `/var/folders/*/*/T/jusprin-shell-*` dir — killed runs leave it behind with the key.

**Give each automated harness run a fresh scratch `$HOME`.** On 2026-09-09 a second run
against a reused scratch `$HOME` (and with a `jusprin-mcp` helper left over from the
first) never got past the Agent page handshake: it printed `HARNESS WAIT
agent_bridge_handshake preview=0 plate=0 slice_valid=1` about twice a second forever and
had to be killed at ten minutes. Runs before and after it, each with a freshly created
`$HOME` and a `pkill -f jusprin-mcp` first, finished with zero `HARNESS WAIT` lines at
all. **The cause was not isolated** — reuse and the stale helper were not separated, so
treat this as a recipe, not an explanation. `rm -rf` and recreate the scratch `$HOME`,
`pkill -f jusprin-mcp`, then run; if the handshake wait appears anyway, kill it early
rather than assuming the change under test broke the bridge.

**2026-09-19 addendum:** background `app_click` on the Home/Agent WKWebViews reports
"ok … unverified" and nothing happens; only display-scope `computer_batch` clicks
reach the page. The re-signed copy opened on the *Built-in Retina Display* while the
display tools default to the Acer, so `switch_display` first. `Return` in the composer
sends in the real app; in the built-in-browser fixture it does not (click the send
button). Another Claude session holding the computer-use lock blocks `request_access`
until Kenneth stops that session. Page-only states are cheaper via [[fake-host-page-fixture]].

**2026-10-28: background clicks no longer open header popups.** In `--manual`, background `app_click` on the printer chip (body or chevron) left the chip pressed but no menu appeared, and `--printer-menu-capture`'s screen blit came back solid black with the screen unlocked (likely a rebuilt binary losing screen-recording permission). For header menu rows, use `HeaderButton::snapshot(2.0)` in the harness instead (see `ring_dashes` in `capture_chip_appearance`).

**Modal dialogs ignore synthetic input (2026-10-28).** OrcaSlicer's own modal dialogs (Send print job, Previously opened file) took no click or key from computer-use in either mode: background app_click is refused ("belongs to a different process") and display clicks/keys do nothing, though log/AX showed the dialog topmost and the app idle. Kenneth's real click on Send worked at once. Web-view screens (Home cards) and menu shortcuts (Cmd+R slice, Cmd+Shift+G send dialog) do work. So when a step needs a modal's button, ask Kenneth to press it and watch the log; don't spend turns on monitors or overlays. Also: launch the copy with `open -n <copy>.app --args --datadir …`, never the binary from the shell (that instance took no input at all), and trim the datadir's `recent_projects` to non-Downloads paths or startup stalls on a macOS Downloads-access prompt.

**Header popups and Open dialogs (2026-11-01).** A background `app_click` on a chip half opens its popup only while the app is frontmost: set frontmost with System Events by unix id, click, find the popup's id with a `CGWindowListCopyWindowInfo` lister (layer 101), then `app_screenshot` that raw id. File > Open's panel belongs to another process, and computer-use refuses input to it and says not to work around that; open the file with the MCP `project_open` tool instead (`load_project(path, "<loadall>")`, against File > Open's `"-"`) and say so. lldb on the RelWithDebInfo build reads and forces flags without touching code: `(Slic3r::GUI::GUI_App*)wxApp::ms_appInstance`, then `preset_bundle->printers.m_edited_preset`; read the Print's flags with a breakpoint on `Print::validate`, because `plater_->p->fff_print` still holds default settings.

name: macos-finder-launch-hides-locale-bugs
description: "On macOS an app opened from Finder/open has no LANG, so the bundled Python resets LC_ALL to C and hides comma-decimal locale bugs; launch with open --env LANG=en_US.UTF-8 to see what Windows users get"
metadata:
  node_type: memory
  type: reference
  originSessionId: dd7b654f-b59a-4190-89ad-3d760bfcdbd4
  modified: 2026-11-16T22:36:21.687Z
---

Found 2026-11-16 while reproducing GitHub issue 39 (Creator 5 Pro had no nozzle sizes in Portuguese; fixed in d010a88c1a by parsing with Orca's `string_to_double_decimal_point`).

wxLocale::Init sets LC_ALL to the app language (e.g. "pt_BR"), so `std::stod`/`strtod`/`snprintf` use a comma. But when the app is started by Finder or plain `open`, the process has no `LANG`, and the bundled Python's startup (`_Py_CoerceLegacyLocale`, C locale coercion) calls `setlocale(LC_ALL, "")`, which resets every category to "C". The bug then vanishes on the Mac. Python documents this coercion as Unix-only, so Windows keeps the comma format; Linux desktops set LANG, so they keep it too.

**How to apply:** to reproduce a locale bug on the Mac, set the language in the scratch conf (`{"app":{"language":"pt_BR"}}`) and launch with `open -n --env LANG=en_US.UTF-8 <app> --args --datadir <scratch>`. Confirm with `lldb -p <pid> --batch -o 'expr (const char*)setlocale(0,(const char*)0)'` (expect "pt_BR/..."). A Finder launch that looks fine is not evidence the bug is absent. Related: [[reproduce-on-real-app-not-fakes]], [[live-test-built-app-on-mac]].

name: scratch-app-driving-traps
description: "Traps met driving a scratch copy of the built app without screen control: in-place binary copy gets SIGKILL, Home drops bridge messages while hidden, header popups need a posted NSEvent, lldb std::string args and @import failures, the model picker needs page JS, a debugger attach once hung a slice."
metadata:
  node_type: memory
  type: reference
  originSessionId: dea8379c-b02c-43a2-a254-4c2259672439
  modified: 2026-11-12T18:04:04.144Z
---

Met while verifying print-host printer window fixes on the scratch `.app` (see [[live-test-built-app-on-mac]], [[open-file-in-app-without-screen-control]]).

- **Copy a new build into a `.app` with `rm` then `cp`.** `cp` over the existing signed binary keeps the inode; the kernel kills the launch at once (exit 137, nothing logged).
- **A launch from a plain Bash call dies when the call ends.** Start the app with `run_in_background: true` and `exec`.
- **Home ignores bridge messages while the main window shows a project.** A queued `launch_monitor` through `JUSPRIN_HOME_DEV_URL` is sent by the page and silently dropped; switch to Home first (`m_tabpanel->SetSelection(0)` via lldb).
- **Background `app_click` does not reach the header's popup menus** (they are not listed as windows). Post the click into the app's queue with lldb: `expr -l objc -- @import AppKit`, then `NSEvent mouseEventWithType:NSEventTypeLeftMouseDown/Up location:NSMakePoint(x, y-from-popup-bottom) ... windowNumber:[popup windowNumber]` and `[NSApp postEvent:atStart:NO]`. Render the popup with `cacheDisplayInRect:` on its contentView ([[capture-mac-popups-for-platform-diff]]).
- **lldb cannot build `std::string` args.** This libc++ uses the alternate short-string layout: a 24-byte char array with the text at offset 0 and its length in byte 23 (≤ 22 chars), passed as `*(std::string*)buf`.
- **wx `wxStaticText::Wrap()` (Orca's wx) skips a width it already wrapped at and keeps the first text it wrapped**, so SetLabel + Wrap on a reused label comes back unwrapped. Use a fresh label.
- **With the screen locked, an instrumented dev page stops polling** (WebKit throttles the hidden page's timers; `document.visibilityState` is "hidden"). Run JS in it through lldb instead: walk `[NSApp windows]` → subviews to the `WKWebView` (match its title or `URL`), then `[webview evaluateJavaScript:@"…" completionHandler:nil]`; the page can `fetch()` results to the dev server. A menu item without a shortcut: `[[item target] performSelector:[item action] withObject:item afterDelay:0.5]` from lldb, so the modal it opens runs after detach.
- **`@import AppKit` can fail silently in lldb `expr`** ("no known method '-windows'"). Then cast everything to `id` and get classes with `((Class(*)(const char*))objc_getClass)("NSApplication")`; a working runner that runs a JS file in the chat panel (title "JusPrin Agent") was `runjs.sh` in the 2026-11-12 scratchpad.
- **The composer's model picker is a drop-down the background `app_click` refuses.** Click it from page JS via the runner above. OpenRouter's list labels models "Anthropic: Claude …", so a regex on "Claude Fable" picks OpenRouter's copy; the Anthropic-key one starts with "Claude".
- **A slice right after lldb attaches hung once (2026-11-12).** The worker sat in upstream `name_tbb_thread_pool_threads_set_locale()`, a barrier every TBB thread must reach, and the main thread waited in `BackgroundSlicingProcess::start()` forever. metadata:

A JusPrin git worktree builds against the already-built deps by configuring:

```
cmake -B build/arm64 -G "Ninja Multi-Config" -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release \
  -DCMAKE_OSX_ARCHITECTURES=arm64 -DCMAKE_OSX_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET=15.0 \
  -DCMAKE_PREFIX_PATH=/Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin/deps/build/arm64/OrcaSlicer_dep/usr/local \
  -DSLIC3R_GUI=ON -DSLIC3R_STATIC=ON -DSLIC3R_PCH=ON -DBUILD_TESTS=ON \
  -DCMAKE_AR=/opt/homebrew/opt/llvm/bin/llvm-ar -DCMAKE_RANLIB=/opt/homebrew/opt/llvm/bin/llvm-ranlib
```

ONE PREFIX PATH (2026-11-15): since the 2.5.0 merge, CMakeLists.txt finds its bundled Python under CMAKE_PREFIX_PATH + /libpython; a two-entry list fails configure with "Bundled Python executable not found under <a;b>/libpython/bin". Pass only the JusPrin deps path (as other worktrees' caches do).

CMAKE BINARY (2026-09-29): configure with `/Applications/CMake.app/Contents/bin/cmake` (put it first on PATH). Homebrew's cmake 4.1 at /opt/homebrew/bin fails with "Could NOT find Eigen3 (missing: EIGEN3_VERSION_OK) (Required is at least version 5.0.1)", and a failed configure poisons the cache: `rm -rf build` before retrying.

The two `CMAKE_AR`/`CMAKE_RANLIB` flags are required on a FRESH build dir:
without them Apple's ar is used and liblibslic3r_gui.a (>4 GiB in
RelWithDebInfo) fails to archive. They only work at first configure, not on
reconfigure. Full story: agent-docs/macos-build-troubleshooting.md. See
[[liblibslic3r-gui-4gib-ar-limit]].

<#
.SYNOPSIS
    Fails when a Windows build has an exception class with broken throw info.

.DESCRIPTION
    Clang on the MSVC ABI can leave the copy constructor out of the CatchableType it emits for
    an exception class that comes through a precompiled header
    (https://github.com/llvm/llvm-project/issues/53486). The linker keeps one throw info per
    class, so when it keeps such a record, a copy of that exception (std::exception_ptr, a catch
    by value) shares its data with the original and the data is freed twice.

    A class is either trivially copyable or not, so a binary should never have both a CatchableType
    without a copy constructor (_CT??_R0?AV<class>@@@8<size>) and one with it
    (_CT??_R0?AV<class>@@@8??0<class>...). The script lists each PDB's public symbols with the
    llvm-pdbutil next to the build's compiler and reports every class that has both.

    scripts\test_check_exception_throw_info.ps1 tests it.

.PARAMETER BuildDir
    The slicer build directory. Its CMakeCache.txt names the compiler, and its src\<Config>
    holds the PDBs to check, which must include OrcaSlicer.pdb.

.PARAMETER Config
    The configuration whose PDBs to check (default: Release).

.PARAMETER Pdb
    PDBs to check instead of the ones in <BuildDir>\src\<Config>, as a list or comma-separated.

.PARAMETER Dump
    Saved `llvm-pdbutil dump --publics` output to check instead of PDBs. Needs no build.

# Fails the build when JusPrin's own code converts a wxString with
# ToStdString(). It converts with wxConvLibc, the encoding of the C library's
# locale. JusPrin's std::strings are UTF-8, but the app can run in the "C"
# locale (macOS starts it so from Finder), and there ToStdString() returns ""
# for any text with a letter outside ASCII, such as a translated label. Use
# std::string(text.ToUTF8()) instead.
#
# Run as: cmake -DJUSPRIN_DIR=<this folder> -DSTAMP=<file> -P CheckWxStringConversions.cmake
file(GLOB_RECURSE sources "${JUSPRIN_DIR}/*.cpp" "${JUSPRIN_DIR}/*.hpp" "${JUSPRIN_DIR}/*.h" "${JUSPRIN_DIR}/*.mm")
list(FILTER sources EXCLUDE REGEX "/node_modules/")
set(found "")
foreach (source IN LISTS sources)
    file(STRINGS "${source}" lines REGEX "ToStdString[ \t]*\\(")
    foreach (line IN LISTS lines)
        file(RELATIVE_PATH name "${JUSPRIN_DIR}" "${source}")
        string(STRIP "${line}" line)
        string(APPEND found "\n  ${name}: ${line}")
    endforeach ()
endforeach ()
if (found)
    message(FATAL_ERROR "JusPrin code calls wxString::ToStdString(), which loses non-ASCII text outside a UTF-8 locale. "
                        "Use std::string(text.ToUTF8()) instead (see CheckWxStringConversions.cmake):${found}")
endif ()
file(TOUCH "${STAMP}")

---
name: windows-gui-test-vm-gcp
description: Working recipe for testing the OrcaSlicer/JusPrin GUI headlessly on a GPU-less Windows VM in GCP, and the four traps that make it fail silently.
metadata:
  type: project
---

A Windows GUI test VM for this app works in GCP with no GPU. Instance
`jusprin-win-test`, project `elegoo-backend`, zone `us-central1-a`,
n2-standard-16 (16 vCPU, 64 GB, Cascade Lake), 500 GB pd-balanced,
Windows Server 2022. Harness + full README live outside the repo
at `/Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin/.claude/vm-harness/windows/`. Verified 2026-09-07 end to end:
launch, screenshot, scripted click, verify the UI advanced.

**Why:** four failure modes here are silent — they look like "the app has no
window" or "the app hung" rather than reporting an error, so they cost hours if
rediscovered from scratch.

**How to apply:**
- OpenGL: the app hard-requires 3.2 and Windows software rendering is 1.1. Drop
  Mesa's `opengl32.dll` + `libgallium_wgl.dll` beside the .exe. Then force
  `GALLIUM_DRIVER=llvmpipe` and `LIBGL_ALWAYS_SOFTWARE=1` — otherwise Mesa picks
  its d3d12 backend (the GCE virtual display exposes a D3D12 device) and crashes
  on the first frame.
- Never copy the whole Mesa .7z to the VM: Defender deletes it as
  Trojan:Win32/Suschil!rfn. Extract the two DLLs elsewhere, copy only those, and
  no AV exclusion is needed.
- Session isolation is the big one: display APIs, EnumWindows and
  MainWindowTitle only see the calling session's window station, so over SSH they
  report nothing and it reads as "no window exists". Run anything UI-touching as a
  scheduled task with `-LogonType Interactive`.
- Auto-logon must be re-applied on every boot; the GCE image clears the Winlogon
  values after the boot that sets them.
- Resolution needs `gcloud compute instances update --enable-display-device`
  (instance must be stopped) or you get 640x480, smaller than the app's own window.
- WebView2 runtime is absent on a clean Windows Server image; without it the app
  blocks on a modal prompt at startup. Matters especially for JusPrin's
  WebView-based UI. See [[jusprin-rebrand-seams]].

Claude Code and the Claude desktop app are both installed for `guitest`
(2026-09-08). CLI: the native Windows installer `irm https://claude.ai/install.ps1`
puts `claude.exe` in `C:\Users\guitest\.local\bin` - no Node needed, the box has
none. Desktop app: install with Anthropic's own Intune script,
`https://downloads.claude.ai/releases/enterprise/intune/Install-Claude.ps1 -Scope User`,
which resolves the official MSIX and verifies its signature and publisher identity.
MSIX deployment works on this Windows Server 2022 image. Launch the packaged app in
session 1 through explorer.exe, so it lands at normal integrity even though the
scheduled task is elevated:
`Invoke-InSession -Exe C:\Windows\explorer.exe -ArgLine "shell:AppsFolder\Claude_pzs8sxrjxfjjc!Claude"`.
Electron renders fine on this GPU-less VM with no flags.

RDP: port 3389 is open project-wide via `default-allow-rdp` (to 0.0.0.0/0 - not
narrowed yet), and RDP as `guitest` reconnects to the existing console session
rather than starting a second one. Run `./get-rdp-password.sh` in the harness to
print the current credentials; it resolves the ephemeral IP itself and verifies
the password actually authenticates before handing it to you. Do NOT use
`gcloud compute reset-windows-password` - autologon.ps1 re-syncs the account to
Winlogon\DefaultPassword at the next boot and would undo it.

The search turned up a known cause: on Windows, `wxConvLibc` converts using the active ANSI code page, so non-ASCII text can be mangled or dropped. Sources are wxWidgets blog posts, the wxWidgets git history, and the wx-dev mailing list.

- **Platform-dependent decoding:** A wxWidgets blog post says the same code can work on one platform and silently lose string contents on another, because encoding or decoding fails without an error. On Windows, `wxConvLibc` may pick a code page such as Windows-1252 in Europe, since Windows has not adopted UTF-8 across the board. (Some users were in fact noticing that the same code was working well on a platform, while on another platform the contents of some strings were lost; the same strings may be decoded incorrectly, because Windows is not currently adopting UTF-8 as standard.)
- **Failure mode:** A separate wxWidgets post notes that with a code page like CP1250 on Windows, converting a wxString to `char*` can fail and leave the result empty. (CP1250 under Microsoft Windows). In this case, conversion of wxString to char* would fail and p would be just empty.)
- **ToStdString:** The `conv` parameter, which defaults to `wxConvLibc`, was added in wxWidgets 3.1.1. The docs describe the output as using the current locale encoding and call the operation potentially destructive. (This parameter is new in wxWidgets 3.1.1.; This is also a potentially destructive operation.)
- **Recommended fix:** The wxWidgets team recommends defining `wxNO_UNSAFE_WXSTRING_CONV` and fixing the resulting compile errors. Converting with UTF-8 instead, via `ToStdString(wxConvUTF8)` or `utf8_str()`, avoids the loss. (Define wxNO_UNSAFE_WXSTRING_CONV for your code and fix the resulting compilation errors to ensure that you don't lose any data; convert wxString to UTF-8 encoding which will never lose data, using methods such as utf8_str().)

If you want to check the exact behavior for your build, the wxWidgets documentation for `wxString::ToStdString` and the `strconv.cpp` source would be the primary references. I did not find a single post that matches your exact error message.

# Windows GUI test VM (GCP) — working harness

Drives a wxWidgets + OpenGL desktop app on a GPU-less Windows VM in GCP,
headlessly: launch it, screenshot it, click it, verify the result.

Verified 2026-09-07 with OrcaSlicer 2.4.2 portable.

## The VM

    instance : jusprin-win-test
    project  : elegoo-backend
    zone     : us-central1-a
    machine  : n2-standard-8, Windows Server 2022, 100GB pd-balanced
    display  : virtual display device ENABLED (required, see below)
    login    : ssh as guitest with ~/.ssh/google_compute_engine

The external IP is ephemeral and CHANGES on every stop/start. Re-read it with:

    gcloud compute instances describe jusprin-win-test --zone=us-central1-a \
      --project=elegoo-backend \
      --format="value(networkInterfaces[0].accessConfigs[0].natIP)"

then update winssh.sh / winscp.sh.

## Four things that had to be solved

1. **OpenGL.** The app hard-requires OpenGL 3.2 (src/slic3r/GUI/OpenGLManager.cpp)
   and exits below it. Stock Windows software rendering reports 1.1. Fix: drop
   Mesa's `opengl32.dll` + `libgallium_wgl.dll` (from pal1000/mesa-dist-win) next
   to the .exe. Reports OpenGL 4.2 on plain CPU.

   Mesa then auto-picks its **d3d12** backend, because the GCE virtual display
   exposes "Microsoft Basic Render Driver" as a D3D12 device — and that path
   crashed on the first frame. run-app.cmd forces the CPU rasterizer with
   `GALLIUM_DRIVER=llvmpipe` and `LIBGL_ALWAYS_SOFTWARE=1`.

   Do NOT copy the whole Mesa .7z onto the VM: Windows Defender flags the archive
   as Trojan:Win32/Suschil!rfn and deletes it. Extract the two DLLs elsewhere and
   copy just those — Defender does not object to them, so no AV exclusion is
   needed. (The archive's sha256 matches GitHub's published release digest; the
   detection is a heuristic on the bundle, which also contains Vulkan layers,
   D3D12 compilers and media-foundation encoders we don't use.)

2. **A visible desktop.** A GUI app started from an SSH shell lands in a session
   with no desktop and screenshots come back black. autologon.ps1 creates a local
   admin `guitest` and sets Winlogon AutoAdminLogon so console session 1 is always
   live. Something in the GCE image clears those values after the boot that sets
   them, so startup.ps1 re-applies them on EVERY boot.

3. **Session isolation.** Display APIs, EnumWindows and Get-Process MainWindowTitle
   only see the CALLING session's window station. Run them over SSH and they
   silently report nothing — which reads as "the app has no window" when it does.
   Everything that touches the UI goes through `Invoke-InSession` in harness.ps1,
   which registers a scheduled task with `-LogonType Interactive` so it runs in
   session 1, and writes its output to a file to be read back over SSH.

4. **Resolution.** Without a GCE virtual display device the guest falls back to
   Microsoft Basic Display Adapter with no EDID = 640x480, and the app's own
   window is 760x500. Fix (requires the instance to be STOPPED):

       gcloud compute instances stop   jusprin-win-test --zone=us-central1-a --project=elegoo-backend

Microsoft Edge WebView2 runtime is NOT present on a clean Windows Server image.
Without it the app puts up a modal "WebView2 Runtime" prompt and startup blocks
forever. Installed here as 152.0.4191.66 via the Evergreen bootstrapper:

    Invoke-WebRequest "https://go.microsoft.com/fwlink/p/?LinkId=2124703" -OutFile setup.exe

This matters more for JusPrin than for stock Orca, since JusPrin's UI is
WebView-based.

# Helper functions for driving a GUI app in the auto-logon console session.
# A process started from an SSH session has no desktop; a scheduled task with
# LogonType Interactive lands in guitest's live session 1 instead.

function Invoke-InSession {
    param([string]$TaskName, [string]$Exe, [string]$ArgLine = "", [string]$WorkDir = "C:\guitest")
    $a = if ($ArgLine) {
        New-ScheduledTaskAction -Execute $Exe -Argument $ArgLine -WorkingDirectory $WorkDir
    } else {

    }
    $p = New-ScheduledTaskPrincipal -UserId "guitest" -LogonType Interactive -RunLevel Highest
    $s = New-ScheduledTaskSettingsSet -AllowStartIfOnBatteries -DontStopIfGoingOnBatteries `
             -ExecutionTimeLimit ([TimeSpan]::Zero)
    Register-ScheduledTask -TaskName $TaskName -Action $a -Principal $p -Settings $s -Force | Out-Null
    Start-ScheduledTask -TaskName $TaskName
}

        -ArgLine "-NoProfile -WindowStyle Hidden -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File C:\guitest\screenshot.ps1"

}

# Runs a helper .ps1 from C:\guitest inside session 1 and waits for it.

# Building JusPrin from source on the Windows VM

Verified 2026-09-07: full build from a clean VM, then run and screenshotted.
Total ~1h10m of machine time on n2-standard-16 (16 vCPU, 64 GB).

    deps build   22.7 min   (all 24 applicable deps from source)
    slicer build 23.0 min
    output       C:\src\JusPrin\build\src\Release\orca-slicer.exe (261 KB launcher)
                 + OrcaSlicer.dll (122.7 MB — the actual application)

## Order of operations

1. `install-buildtools.ps1` — CMake 4.3.5 (CI pins ~4.3.0), Ninja, Git for
   Windows, Strawberry Perl, and VS 2022 Build Tools with the VCTools workload.
2. Clone the repo (public, no credentials needed). Shallow is fine: the version
   comes from `version.inc`, not git tags.
3. `build-deps-full.ps1` — builds all deps. **Do not use the CI dependency
   artifact**; see below.
4. `build-slicer.ps1` — runs `build_release_vs.bat slicer`.
5. Put Mesa where the app looks for it, then `run-jusprin.cmd`.

## Things that will bite you

**Run long builds as a SCHEDULED TASK, not over SSH.** Windows OpenSSH kills the
whole process tree when the session ends, so a build started from an SSH command
(even detached with Start-Process) dies on disconnect. Register it instead:

    New-ScheduledTaskPrincipal -UserId "SYSTEM" -LogonType ServiceAccount -RunLevel Highest

Two builds racing in one directory corrupt each other — OpenSSL failed with
`C1033: cannot open program database ossl_static.pdb` when that happened here.

**awk must be on PATH.** `deps/PNG/PNG.cmake` passes `-DPNG_PREFIX=prusaslicer_`,
so libpng generates `pngprefix.h` with an awk script. Without awk you get
`AWK-NOTFOUND` in the PNG CMakeCache and then `C1083: Cannot open include file:
'pngprefix.h'`. Git for Windows ships awk — add `C:\Program Files\Git\usr\bin`
to PATH, not just `C:\Program Files\Git\cmd`.

**Set `CMAKE_POLICY_VERSION_MINIMUM=3.5`.** Several bundled CMakeLists still
declare pre-3.5 minimums, which CMake 4.x rejects outright.

**The CI dependency artifact is unusable.** `OrcaSlicer_dep_win64_20260906`
contains a bundle built 2025-10-17, before `deps/Eigen` was added. The source
requires Eigen 5.0.1 and CMake fails at configure with "Could not find a package
configuration file provided by Eigen3". Build deps from source instead.

**Never hard-stop the VM mid-build.** Stopping the instance during the deps build
left 622 of 22,011 installed files as NUL bytes. It surfaced as bogus syntax
errors deep in Boost headers. Detect it with:

    Get-ChildItem $prefix -Recurse -Include *.hpp,*.h,*.cmake |
      # read first 4 KB, flag any file containing byte 0

The fix is a clean rebuild; DL_CACHE keeps all 21 source archives, so it is a
recompile, not a re-download.

**Qhull is expected to be missing.** `deps/CMakeLists.txt` comments it out under
`if (MSVC)` ("Experimental"), so 24 built deps is the complete set on Windows.

## Running it — use the app's own Mesa hook

Do NOT drop opengl32.dll next to the exe. `src/OrcaSlicer_app_msvc.cpp` already
handles this: when system OpenGL is below 2.0 it loads `<exedir>\mesa\opengl32.dll`
itself and prints "MESA OpenGL library was loaded successfully".

    build\src\Release\mesa\opengl32.dll      <- Mesa's, the app loads this
    build\src\Release\libgallium_wgl.dll     <- dependency, resolves from exe dir

Still export `GALLIUM_DRIVER=llvmpipe` and `LIBGL_ALWAYS_SOFTWARE=1`: the GCE
virtual display exposes a D3D12 device, and Mesa's d3d12 backend crashes on the
first rendered frame.

## Windows CI is broken for a different reason

`Build all`'s Windows job fails at `cmake -G "Visual Studio 17 2022"` with
"could not find any instance of Visual Studio". That is NOT a bug in
`build_release_vs.bat` — the same script picks generator VS 17 2022 here from
`msbuild -version` (17.14.51.32402) and configures fine against a registered
Build Tools instance. The problem is the GitHub runner's environment.
$ErrorActionPreference = "Stop"
$ProgressPreference = "SilentlyContinue"
function Log($m) { Write-Host "[INSTALL] $m" }
$root = "C:\guitest"

$appUrl = "https://github.com/SoftFever/OrcaSlicer/releases/download/v2.4.2/OrcaSlicer_Windows_V2.4.2_x64_portable.zip"
if (-not (Test-Path "$root\app")) {
    Log "Downloading OrcaSlicer 2.4.2 portable (~171MB)"
    Invoke-WebRequest -Uri $appUrl -OutFile "$root\app.zip"
    Log "Downloaded $((Get-Item "$root\app.zip").Length) bytes; extracting"
    Expand-Archive -Path "$root\app.zip" -DestinationPath "$root\app" -Force
}

$exe = Get-ChildItem -Path "$root\app" -Filter "*.exe" -Recurse |
       Where-Object { $_.Name -match "orca" -and $_.Name -notmatch "vcredist|unins" } |
       Sort-Object Length -Descending | Select-Object -First 1

input.recap: The bug reproduces in JusPrin 2.0.1 on Windows in German: Ask AI about filament settings fails with an invalid-UTF-8 error. The fix isn't verified on Windows yet, because the test VM's disk is full. The Mac build of the fix is still running.
input.ask: How should I free space on the Windows VM for the fix build?

content.text:
The bug reproduces in the real JusPrin 2.0.1 on Windows. With the app set to German, I opened a project and chose the filament menu's "Ask AI about filament settings…" ("KI zu Filamenteinstellungen fragen…"). The chat opened empty with "Bei uns ist etwas schiefgelaufen", the generic "something went wrong on our side" error. The report's details say:

```
class Slic3r::RuntimeError: jusprin-agent-bridge: hello w-1: [json.exception.type_error.316] invalid UTF-8 byte at index 3: 0xFC
```

0xFC is "ü" in Windows-1252. The back button's label "Zurück zu „Vorbereiten“" reached the JSON writer as Windows-1252 bytes instead of UTF-8, which matches what I predicted. So on Windows in German, and likely in every language whose label has a letter outside ASCII, the filament chat doesn't work at all. I sent you the screenshot, and I closed the dialog without sending the report.

I haven't confirmed the fix on Windows yet. My Windows build of 2.0.1 plus the fix stopped because the VM's disk is full: 0.57 GB free of 500 GB. I removed only my own partial build and download. The space is held by other sessions' leftovers:

| Folder | Size | Last changed |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `C:\b` (a worktree at an October 20 commit) | 218 GB | Nov 8 |
| `C:\src\jd` | 34 GB | Nov 11 |
| `release-2.0.1` worktree's build | 32 GB | Nov 18 |
| `C:\src\JusPrin\build` | 31 GB | Nov 17 |
| `import-menu` worktree's build | 23 GB | Nov 12 |
| `issue39` worktree's build | 21 GB | Nov 16 |
| Codex worktrees | 18 GB | Oct 1 |

**Decision needed: how to make room on the Windows test VM for one build of about 30 GB.**
- **Grow the disk (my pick).** I'd add 100 GB to the VM's disk in GCP, then extend the C: partition. It costs about $10 a month more and can't be shrunk later, but deletes nothing anyone might still need.
- **Delete `C:\b`.** It frees 218 GB at no cost. It's a worktree at an October 20 commit, untouched since November 8, but I can't tell whether a session or Kenneth still wants it.

The Mac build of the fix is still running (about 1,045 of 1,144 steps). When it finishes I'll run the JusPrin tests on it. Nothing is committed: the change sits in `/Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin/.claude/worktrees/tostdstring-utf8` on branch `tostdstring-utf8`, plus a patched copy on the VM.

I built 2.0.1 plus the fix on the VM and repeated the steps that failed: German app, open the 20mm_cube project, then the filament menu's "KI zu Filamenteinstellungen fragen…" (Ask AI about filament settings). The filament chat now opens normally, titled "Einstellungen für Generic PA", with no error dialog. On the released 2.0.1, the same steps showed the "invalid UTF-8 byte 0xFC" failure. I sent you both screenshots.

The chat's first line is still English: "I can help with settings for Generic PA in slot 1…". That's the unmarked filament-chat opening line from the translation audit, a separate problem this change doesn't touch.

I couldn't capture the close button's tooltip in a screenshot, so I haven't seen the German label itself on screen. What I did confirm is that the label no longer breaks the JSON message that carries it.

**What else was done to get there:**
- I grew the VM's disk from 500 GB to 600 GB and extended C:. It now has 81 GB free.
- The VM has no Python, so its builds skip the native translation catalogs. That includes the 2.0.1 build another session made there. I copied the released 2.0.1 catalogs into my build; it's the same commit, so the strings match.
- The new check ran during the Windows build too.

**Left in place:**
- My Windows build, about 30 GB, at `C:\src\JusPrin\.claude\worktrees\utf8-fix` on the VM, in case a retest is needed. I'll remove it once this lands.
- The 2.0.1 copy and its German settings folder in `C:\guitest\utf8`.
- On the Mac, the change itself, still uncommitted, in `/Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin/.claude/worktrees/tostdstring-utf8` on branch `tostdstring-utf8`.
Commit and land

--- Home shows a card when a new JusPrin version is out
JusPrin 2.0.0 found 2.0.1 but told nobody: the update check's answer
showed only in Preferences > Updates, which few people open. Home now
leads its right column with a card while the check has a newer release
to offer (board update-07 on the JusPrin v2 canvas):

- "JusPrin 2.0.1 is available", the version running, and that projects,
  printers, settings and a running print are unaffected by installing.
- See what's new opens Preferences > Updates, which shows the notes.
- Open download page opens the release page on GitHub, as Preferences'
  Download does; JusPrin downloads nothing itself. The card stays until
  the new version runs.
- Remind me tomorrow hides the card for a day
  (jusprin_update_remind_after). Skip this version is Preferences' Skip.

No card when automatic checks are off, in stealth mode, or for a
Microsoft Store install. Home's poll compares the card with the one it
last sent, so the card comes and goes with the check's answers and with
the reminder running out.

The card's text passed a cold-reader check on the board. Translations
for the new strings are machine-made and marked; Basque, Thai and
Lithuanian are also marked for review. The guide's Updates section
names the card.

   - **The bug.** `wxString::ToStdString()` defaults to `wxConvLibc`, the C library's locale encoding. On Windows that is the ANSI code page (Windows-1252), so German "Zurück zu „Vorbereiten“" becomes non-UTF-8 bytes, and nlohmann json throws `type_error.316`.
   - **Why the Mac never showed it.** The bundled Python's locale coercion sets LC_CTYPE=C.UTF-8 on a Finder-style launch. Only the plain "C" locale gives an empty string.
   - **Fix pattern:** `std::string(x.ToUTF8())`.
   - **The check** is a CMake `-P` script, run by `add_custom_command` with a stamp file, depending on a `CONFIGURE_DEPENDS` glob of the JusPrin sources. `add_dependencies(libslic3r_gui jusprin-wxstring-conversions)` makes it run before the GUI library compiles.

     # locale, while JusPrin's std::strings are UTF-8. On Windows that encoding is

     # ToStdString() returns "" for any text with a letter outside ASCII, such as a
     # translated label. Use std::string(text.ToUTF8()) instead.

     # Run as: cmake -DJUSPRIN_DIR=<this folder> -DSTAMP=<file> -P CheckWxStringConversions.cmake
     file(GLOB_RECURSE sources "${JUSPRIN_DIR}/*.cpp" "${JUSPRIN_DIR}/*.hpp" "${JUSPRIN_DIR}/*.h" "${JUSPRIN_DIR}/*.mm")
     list(FILTER sources EXCLUDE REGEX "/node_modules/")
     set(found "")
     foreach (source IN LISTS sources)
         file(STRINGS "${source}" lines REGEX "ToStdString[ \t]*\\(")
         foreach (line IN LISTS lines)

             string(STRIP "${line}" line)
             string(APPEND found "\n  ${name}: ${line}")
         endforeach ()
     endforeach ()
     if (found)

                             "Use std::string(text.ToUTF8()) instead (see CheckWxStringConversions.cmake):${found}")
     endif ()
     file(TOUCH "${STAMP}")

                 -P "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/CheckWxStringConversions.cmake"
         DEPENDS ${jusprin_checked_sources} "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/CheckWxStringConversions.cmake"
         COMMENT "Checking JusPrin's wxString conversions"

     add_custom_target(jusprin-wxstring-conversions DEPENDS "${jusprin_conversion_stamp}")

The fix is committed on your local `jusprin-dev` as `04def74276`, "Filament chat opens on Windows in every language: convert wxString to UTF-8". Nothing is pushed yet: `origin/jusprin-dev` is still at `92e4b3dc69`.

**The problem:** on German Windows, clicking "KI zu Filamenteinstellungen fragen…" opened an empty chat with "Bei uns ist etwas schiefgelaufen". The app converted a translated label to text with `ToStdString()`. On Windows that produces the system's old code page (Windows-1252), not UTF-8, so the "ü" in "Zurück" made the JSON library refuse the text.

**What changed:**
- All 11 `ToStdString()` calls in the fork's own code under `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/` now use `std::string(x.ToUTF8())`. Upstream-owned code is untouched.
- A new check, `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/CheckWxStringConversions.cmake`, runs before the GUI library compiles. The build fails if a `ToStdString(` call appears in that folder again.

**What I tested:**
- **Windows VM, before:** released 2.0.1 in German showed the error.
- **Windows VM, after:** the same build with the fix opened the filament chat with no error. Its first line is still in English, which is one of the separate untranslated strings listed in `i18n-unmarked-strings.md`.
- **Mac:** `jusprin_tests` all pass.
- **The check:** it stops the build when I add a `ToStdString` call and passes once the call is removed. It also passes on the landed tree.

**Cleanup:** the Mac worktree and its branch `tostdstring-utf8` are deleted. On the Windows VM, the fix worktree, the copy of 2.0.1 and my scheduled tasks are removed, and the disk, now grown to 600 GB, has 102 GB free.

I couldn't tell the session that relayed Kenneth's request, because it is archived.
